title: Electrodynamic tether reliability for deorbit
bottleneck: Electrodynamic tethers — long conductive cables generating drag from Earth's magnetic field — could deorbit satellites without propellant, but deploying a kilometer-long tether reliably is notoriously hard: tethers snag, sever on micrometeorites, and induce dynamics that can destabilize the host. Past flights left a legacy of skepticism after breakages and underperformance. A deorbit device must work years after launch on a dead satellite — the worst possible reliability case.
why_it_blocks: Propellantless deorbit is the cheapest compliance path for coming disposal rules; if tethers cannot be trusted, operators must reserve propellant or add thrusters — mass and cost someone must pay.
current_state: Japanese and European teams continue tether experiments; JAXA's KITE demo had partial success. No tether has operationally deorbited a satellite.
